train.message:
fix(q6k): PAR-066 Fix CoalescedQ6K scale alignment for byte loads

Five-Whys root cause analysis:
- Why 1: CoalescedQ6K kernel crashes with CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN (716)
- Why 2: Memory access error detected by compute-sanitizer
- Why 3: Misaligned 4-byte (u32) loads on scale data
- Why 4: Q6K super-blocks are 210 bytes (NOT 4-byte aligned)
- Why 5 (ROOT CAUSE): Scales at offset 192, row 1 gives 402 bytes, 402 % 4 = 2

Fix: Changed from 4x ld_global_u32 loads to 16x ld_global_u8 byte loads
with warp shuffle broadcast to share scales across all 32 lanes.

Performance: Now matches original Q6K correctness (max diff 0.00001)
Enabled for all aligned K dimensions (K % 256 == 0)

Refs SHOWCASE-BRICK-001

train.message:
fix(gguf): PAR-126 Fix scratch path bugs for correct generation

Two critical bugs fixed in zero-allocation inference paths:

1. GQA dimension bug in forward_single_with_scratch:
   - OLD: Used layer.qkv_weight.q_dim() which returns out_dim/3
   - PROBLEM: For GQA (e.g., Qwen with 12 heads, 2 kv_heads), this gave
     wrong dimensions: 2560/3=853 instead of q_dim=1536, k_dim=256
   - FIX: Use config to compute correct dimensions like forward_single_with_cache

2. Loop structure bug in generate_with_scratch:
   - OLD: Called forward() BEFORE sampling on each iteration
   - PROBLEM: First iteration re-processed last prompt token at wrong position,
     corrupting KV cache and producing wrong output
   - FIX: Match generate_with_cache structure - sample first (using prefill
     logits), then forward the new token for next iteration

Verified: generate_with_scratch now produces identical output to
generate_with_cache (bench_scratch passes).

Refs: PAR-126

fix(gguf): Correct RoPE rotation and tokenizer for LLaMA models

Root cause analysis (five-whys):
1. Why wrong output? Logits were incorrect (token "1" > token "2" for "1+1=")
2. Why wrong logits? Attention computation was incorrect
3. Why wrong attention? RoPE rotation used wrong style
4. Why wrong RoPE? Used NEOX (split halves) instead of NORM (adjacent pairs)
5. Why NEOX? No rope_type detection - assumed all models use NEOX

Fixes:
- Add rope_type field to GGUFConfig (0=NORM, 2=NEOX)
- Read rope_type from GGUF metadata
- Fix apply_rope() in both QuantizedGGUFTransformer and OwnedQuantizedModel
- NORM style: rotates (x[0],x[1]), (x[2],x[3]) - used by LLaMA
- NEOX style: rotates (x[0],x[half]), (x[1],x[half+1]) - used by GPT-NeoX

Tokenizer fix:
- SentencePiece models prepend space before tokenization
- "1+1=" → " 1+1=" → "▁1+1=" (6 tokens, matching llama.cpp)

Verified correct output:
- "1+1=" → "2" (was "1")
- "2+2=" → "4" (was newline)

train.message:
fix(gqa): Support GQA models in KV cache forward pass

EXTREME TDD fix for Grouped Query Attention (GQA) models in KV cache:

Problem:
- forward_single_with_cache and forward_with_cache assumed Q/K/V have
  equal sizes (hidden_dim), but GQA models have smaller K/V dimensions
- Caused panic: "range end index X out of range for slice of length Y"
- Affected models: Qwen2 (14 heads, 2 KV heads), TinyLlama (32 heads, 4 KV heads)

Solution:
- Calculate kv_dim = num_kv_heads * head_dim for proper QKV extraction
- Extract Q: [0..hidden_dim], K: [hidden_dim..hidden_dim+kv_dim],
  V: [hidden_dim+kv_dim..hidden_dim+2*kv_dim]
- Apply RoPE with num_kv_heads for K (not num_heads)
- Use attention_with_cache_gqa for GQA-aware attention computation
- Handle first token case with proper V expansion for all Q heads

Changes:
- src/gguf.rs: Fix forward_single_with_cache QKV extraction and RoPE
- src/apr_transformer.rs: Fix forward_with_cache QKV extraction
- src/apr_transformer.rs: Add empty_gqa() for GQA-sized layers
- src/apr_transformer.rs: Add GQA KV cache tests (IMP-GQA-001)
- examples/bench_toks.rs: Add KV cache benchmark example

Performance improvement:
- TinyLlama: 1.1 tok/s → 14.9 tok/s (13.5x speedup with KV cache)
- Qwen2.5: 1.0 tok/s → 1.7 tok/s (cache working, needs optimization)

test.message:
feat(perf): Complete Popperian falsification of trueno capabilities (IMP-600 to IMP-802)

- IMP-600: GPU capability falsification
  - GPU 2.7x SLOWER than SIMD for MATVEC (token generation)
  - GPU 57x FASTER for GEMM (batch processing)
  - Added gpu_matvec_benchmark.rs and gpu_gemm_benchmark.rs

- IMP-700: Real-world verification against Ollama
  - Measured: Ollama 240.1 tok/s, Realizar 0.22 tok/s
  - Verified gap: 1,090x (not theoretical)
  - Added imp_700_realworld_verification.rs

- IMP-800: KV cache falsification
  - trueno-db MemoryKvStore provides 128x average speedup
  - Range: 4.5x (short seq) to 512x (long seq)
  - Added imp_800_kv_cache_falsification.rs

- IMP-801: FlashAttention CUDA falsification
  - trueno-gpu FlashAttention provides 16x conservative speedup
  - Scales with sequence length (2x at 128, 32x at 2048)
  - Added imp_801_flash_attention_falsification.rs

- IMP-802: Combined path to parity documented
  - Step 1: KV cache → 8.5x gap
  - Step 2: FlashAttention → ~5x gap
  - Step 3: Q4_K quantized → ~1.25x (PARITY)

All components exist in trueno ecosystem - work is INTEGRATION, not implementation.

Also fixed various clippy lints:
- Added module-level allow for many_single_char_names and similar_names in gguf.rs
- Added lib.rs allow for missing_errors_doc and items_after_statements
- Fixed unused variables and dead code warnings

Spec updated to v3.4.0. All 2025 tests pass.

Refs PERF-PARITY-001

test.message:
feat(gpu): Add M29-M32 production hardening (error recovery, pooling, circuit breakers, logging)

Implements Phase 20-23 of GPU Performance Parity specification:

M29 - Error Recovery & Graceful Degradation (IMP-070, IMP-071, IMP-072):
- ErrorRecoveryStrategy with exponential backoff and jitter
- DegradationManager for GPU→CPU fallback under memory pressure
- FailureIsolator with circuit breaker pattern

M30 - Connection Pooling & Resource Limits (IMP-073, IMP-074, IMP-075):
- ConnectionPool with bounded capacity and health checking
- ResourceLimiter with memory/compute time/queue depth limits
- ResourceMonitor with real-time metrics and snapshots

M31 - Retry Logic & Circuit Breakers (IMP-076, IMP-077, IMP-078):
- RetryPolicy with configurable policies per error type
- CircuitBreaker with Closed/Open/Half-Open states
- BulkheadManager for isolated resource pools per request type

M32 - Production Logging & Diagnostics (IMP-079, IMP-080, IMP-081):
- Logger with structured JSON output and correlation IDs
- PhaseTimer/MemoryTracker/DiagnosticsCollector for latency breakdown
- DebugMode with request capture/replay and state dumps

All 12 new tests passing (IMP-070 through IMP-081).
Zero clippy warnings.

Refs PERF-PARITY-001
